rules.rule:
VantaDB durability rules (source of truth: .opencode/rules/durability.md — En revisión; this is a review checklist, the file is normative).
- Backend KV config (Fjall default, RocksDB opt-in) MUST be justified against the real access pattern: frequent small writes + random reads (vectors live in VantaFile/mmap, NOT in the backend). No compaction/memtable/cache change without a before/after bench vs benches/backend_compare.rs (random_get, seed 42) whose dataset exceeds the cache under test; any backend config change requires an ADR citing pattern + bench.
- Do NOT introduce a complex buffer cache or physical-locality data layout without a measurement vs benches/vfile_search.rs justifying the complexity cost (reopen signal: >15%). LSM + multi-level storage tradeoff is accepted (INV-012 WONTFIX).
- Flag cross-area overlap: indexes → indexes.md, async/locks → concurrency-async.md, public API → api-contract.md.

VantaDB index rules (source of truth: .opencode/rules/indexes.md; this is a review checklist, the file is normative).
- Competitive metrics MUST be honest: no placeholders, no invented numbers — every claimed figure traces to a reproducible bench + command + environment.
- HNSW/distance/topology changes need before/after evidence vs the canonical bench (see docs/operations/BENCHMARKS.md); no silent recall/latency regressions.

VantaDB query-DSL rules (source of truth: .opencode/rules/query-dsl.md; this is a review checklist, the file is normative).
- Quoted phrases = strict adjacency (slop=0); phrase tokenization is literal — no stopwords, no stemming.
- Do NOT add tantivy: custom storage already covers the scope.
- The parser delegates phrases to the planner — no duplicated grammar.

VantaDB memory-budget rules (source of truth: .opencode/rules/memory-budget.md; this is a review checklist, the file is normative).
- Know what lives in RAM vs disk (normative inventory); measure real process RSS, not partial estimates.
- Back-pressure BEFORE the OS OOM-kills the process; every new resident structure declares a cap.

VantaDB concurrency rules (source of truth: .opencode/rules/concurrency-async.md; this is a review checklist, the file is normative).
- Heavy engine work inside async handlers MUST go in spawn_blocking; engine work in MCP/HTTP handlers is ALWAYS spawn_blocking.
- NEVER hold a sync mutex guard across .await; server concurrency via tokio::sync::Semaphore + pool.
- Multi-index coordination: global lock order + *_locked variants; audit deadlocks/data-races on multi-index paths before close.

VantaDB core-engine rules (source of truth: .opencode/rules/core-engine.md; this is a review checklist, the file is normative).
- Experimental features behind `experimental-*` gates, no dependencies in default features.
- Internal functions without callers stay internal — do not export to the SDK.
- No unwrap/expect outside tests (use ? or expect with context); every unsafe requires // SAFETY: + documented invariant.

VantaDB API-contract rules (source of truth: .opencode/rules/api-contract.md; this is a review checklist, the file is normative).
- Every API claim in docs MUST point to a real symbol; single version reference (= workspace version); exact file refs in docs.
- Do not expose in bindings/MCP what the core rejects by default; MCP tools / HTTP endpoints parity code↔docs in the SAME PR.
- Growing public enums require #[non_exhaustive]; no cfg(feature)-gated pub struct fields; business logic lives in core — bindings are glue + memory.

VantaDB server/MCP rules (source of truth: .opencode/rules/server-mcp.md; this is a review checklist, the file is normative).
- serverInfo/versions coherent between docs and code; handler concurrency via semaphore + spawn_blocking.
- /metrics observability MUST be real fed metrics, no placeholders.

VantaDB Python-binding rules (source of truth: .opencode/rules/python-bindings.md; this is a review checklist, the file is normative).
- Eager GIL release on batch ops + Rayon + fail-fast; binding closure ends in the binding, never in core/wrapper.

VantaDB JS-ecosystem rules (source of truth: .opencode/rules/js-ecosystem.md; this is a review checklist, the file is normative).
- WASM persistence IDB/OPFS only via explicit backends; NEVER commit pkg/ or build artifacts.
- Standalone (napi-rs) crates outside the workspace are intentional; binding lifecycle: op-gate + drain on close.

VantaDB frontend-web rules (source of truth: .opencode/rules/frontend-web.md; this is a review checklist, the file is normative).
- Errors via native error.tsx (no external libs); remove dead deps found in audits; JSON-LD hand-emitted in a Server Component.
- Light-only by design (no dark mode); 44px minimum touch targets on mobile; motion tokens only (no hardcoded easing/durations); custom utilities prefix--modifier only in variant families.

VantaDB open-core licensing rules (source of truth: .opencode/rules/open-core-licensing.md; this is a review checklist, the file is normative).
- Core `vantadb` stays Apache-2.0 and gains NO Pro-only features; the Pro crate/edition lives OUTSIDE the workspace (never add to [workspace] members).
- Delivery is compiled artifacts only, never source; per-node offline license validation. cargo-deny (MIT/Apache-2.0) gates the core only.

VantaDB release/CI rules (source of truth: .opencode/rules/release-ci.md; this is a review checklist, the file is normative).
- Production binaries with custom allocator per platform (mimalloc Windows, jemalloc linux/macOS; NEVER jemalloc on Windows).
- sccache only via .github/actions/rust-setup (no per-workflow steps, no cargo install nextest in jobs).
- Dockerfile RUST_VERSION >= workspace rust-version with COPYs pointing at existing dirs; docs/packaging versions = [workspace.package] version.
- No new continue-on-error without a # CATEGORY: tag (EXPERIMENTAL/BEST-EFFORT/NON-CRITICAL/INFORMATIONAL) + flaky issue (AGENTS.md Regla 2).
